title: A little closer to the GPU
subtitle: Particles, instances, shaders, and performance.

lessons.title: A thousand little points
body: THREE.Points draws a set of points using one geometry and one material. It is a good fit for stars, dust, and simple particle clouds where a full mesh per particle would be wasteful.

The position attribute stores one XYZ position for each point. PointsMaterial controls their color and size. With sizeAttenuation enabled by default, points shrink with distance under a perspective camera. Hardware limits the maximum point size.
lessons.hint: Add or edit the final material.size assignment.

quiz.question: Which class renders this point cloud?
quiz.explanation: Points renders point primitives from geometry attributes.

lessons.title: Many objects, fewer draw calls
body: Many separate meshes can mean many draw calls, even when they share a shape and material. InstancedMesh batches repeated geometry with a different transform per instance.

Use a temporary Object3D to build each transform matrix, then copy it with setMatrixAt. Mark instanceMatrix.needsUpdate after editing. Instancing reduces draw-call overhead, but more instances still increase the number of rendered triangles.
lessons.hint: The loop will arrange all instances around a ring.

quiz.question: Instancing primarily reduces…
quiz.explanation: Repeated geometry can be submitted together while each instance keeps its own transform.

lessons.title: Move vertices on the GPU
body: A vertex shader runs on the GPU to position vertices. The fragment shader then determines surface colors. ShaderMaterial lets you write these stages in GLSL.

Uniforms carry shared values from JavaScript into the shader. Our shader displaces each vertex using a sine wave, but its amplitude starts at zero. Increase uAmplitude to reveal the wave. The plane has enough subdivisions for the curve to appear smooth.
lessons.hint: Edit the JavaScript uniform assignment at the bottom. You do not need to rewrite the GLSL.

quiz.question: A uniform is…
options: A value shared across a shader draw
quiz.explanation: Uniforms provide values such as time, colors, and transformation parameters to shaders.

lessons.title: Paint pixels with a formula
body: A fragment shader computes the output for fragments of a rasterized surface. A varying carries per-vertex values into that stage, interpolated across triangles.

We pass UVs as vUv, then use its X component to blend two colors. The GLSL mix function is linear interpolation. Enable the gradient by raising uMix to 1. The included output chunks keep tone mapping and color conversion consistent with the renderer.
lessons.hint: At 0 the whole plane is purple. At 1 it blends toward mint across U.

quiz.question: A varying is interpolated…
quiz.explanation: The rasterizer interpolates vertex outputs for fragments across a primitive.

lessons.title: Spend pixels wisely
body: A high-density screen can render several physical pixels for each CSS pixel. A pixel ratio of 2 doubles each dimension and therefore draws four times as many pixels as a ratio of 1.

Cap pixel ratio to balance sharpness and GPU cost. The preview also reports draw calls and triangle count; these are useful clues, not a complete benchmark. Profile your own scenes before reducing detail or adding expensive effects.

quiz.question: Pixel ratio 2 draws how many times as many pixels as ratio 1?
